flags.derivation: p=0.999, n=1000: p(1-p)/n = 0.000999/1000 = 9.99e-7; sqrt = 0.0009995. f(q)=phi(3.0902)=0.003367. se = 0.0009995/0.003367 = 0.2968 (python: 0.29684). 95% se = 0.06682. Ratio = 0.2968/0.0668 = 4.44, not 14. The source's 0.938 appears to come from sqrt(0.000999)/0.00337 = 9.38 with a misplaced decimal (i.e. forgetting to divide by n, then shifting by 10). Conclusion (precision worse at 99.9%) still holds.

flags.derivation: With empirical quantiles on the y-axis and the reference line fitted through the centre, a light-tailed sample has extremes less extreme than the reference predicts: the lowest empirical quantiles sit ABOVE the line and the highest sit BELOW it. The ends still depart from the line (inward, flattening toward horizontal); they do not bend 'toward the line', which the points in the middle already lie on. The phrase invites the reading 'lighter tails = ends closer to the line', which is not what the plot shows. Key (a) unaffected.
